material_findings.title: DHS launches Ready, Set...ID the Biothreat AI prize challenge
material_findings.summary: USA.gov lists a new DHS three-stage AI-assisted algorithmic biodetection challenge running September 8 through October 14, 2026 with $999,990 in total cash prizes. A DHS September 9 launch announcement says the challenge seeks algorithms that detect known, novel, and unknown biological threats in environmental metagenomic data and gives high-level U.S. eligibility requirements.
material_findings.eligibility_and_cost: DHS's launch announcement says eligible individual entrants must be at least 18 and be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents at submission; eligible entities must be legally incorporated in the United States with their primary place of business in the United States. No entry fee was identified on the official federal listing. Complete rules must still be reviewed for team, employee, contractor, conflict-of-interest, residency, and other exclusions.
material_findings.prize_and_deadline_evidence: USA.gov states total cash prizes of $999,990, a start date of September 8, 2026 at 9:30 AM ET, and an end date of October 14, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET. DHS says the competition has proposal evaluation, prototype development/testing, and final blinded validation stages and that finalists may receive awards as they advance. Stage-by-stage award allocation is not yet preserved in this repository contribution.
material_findings.scope_and_safety: This is a prize-competition discovery finding, not authorization to test any external system and not a directive to develop harmful biological capability. Any future work must remain inside competition-provided datasets/rules and should be limited to defensive detection/classification objectives. Complete DHS rules, dataset handling terms, biosafety constraints, IP/data licenses, judging criteria, and submission requirements must be independently reviewed before an active case is created.
material_findings.recommended_action: Build/Integration should keep this as a high-value opportunity lead until chronology reaches Sep. 10 afternoon. At that point, reopen the DHS host and complete rules, preserve stage payouts, judging/submission requirements, data/IP terms and all eligibility exclusions, then decide whether a narrowly scoped defensive algorithm-development case is appropriate.
